id: The Poet Ridiculed by Hysterical Academics

prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Is it, then, your opinion Women are putty in your hands? Is this the face to launch upon A thousand one night stands? First, please, would you be so kind As to define your contribution To modern verse, the Western mind And human institutions? Where, where is the long, flowing hair, The velvet suit, the broad bow tie; Where is the other-worldly air, Where the abstracted eye? Describe the influence on your verse Of Oscar Mudwarp’s mighty line, The theories of Susan Schmersch Or the spondee’s decline. You’ve labored to present us with This mouse-sized volume; shall this equal The epic glories of Joe Smith? He’s just brought out a sequel. Where are the beard, the bongo drums, Tattered T-shirt and grubby sandals, As who, released from Iowa, comes To tell of wondrous scandals? Have you subversive, out of date, Or controversial ideas? And can you really pull your weight Among such minds as these? Ah, what avails the tenure race, Ah, what the Ph.D., When all departments have a place For nincompoops like thee?

outputs.L1:
Here are two options to elevate the text depending on your intended format. 

### Option 1: Elevated Poetic Satire (Retains the Original Meter and Verse)
*This version refines the vocabulary, rhythm, and classical literary tone while preserving the original poetic structure and sharp satirical wit.*

Is it your firm belief that women are so easily molded by your hand? 
Is this truly the visage destined to launch a thousand fleeting affairs? 
First, would you be so gracious as to define your exact contribution 
To modern poetics, Western thought, and human institutions?

Where, pray tell, is the cascading hair, the velvet attire, the broad bow tie? 
Where is the ethereal, otherworldly presence, and the thoughtfully distant gaze? 
Elaborate on the influence upon your verse of Oscar Mudwarp’s formidable line, 
The critical theories of Susan Schmersch, or the tragic decline of the spondee.

You have labored so mightily to present us with this meager, diminutive volume; 
Does it genuinely presume to match the epic grandiosity of Joe Smith—
Who has, in fact, just published his sequel?

Where are the beatnik beard, the bongo drums, the tattered shirt, and unkempt sandals—
The hallmark of one newly liberated from Iowa, eager to divulge sensational scandals? 
Do you possess any truly subversive, unorthodox, or provocative ideas? 
And are you genuinely equipped to hold your own among intellects of such stature?

Alas, of what value is the arduous pursuit of tenure, 
And what worth lies in the coveted Ph.D., 
When academic departments reserve a place 
For foolish intellects such as thee?

***

### Option 2: High-Register Prose Critique (For a Speech, Review, or Essay)
*This version converts the satire into eloquent, sophisticated academic prose.*

Do you genuinely believe that women are mere putty in your hands, and is that face truly meant to inspire a thousand fleeting encounters? Before proceeding, perhaps you would be so kind as to articulate your precise contributions to contemporary poetry, the Western intellectual tradition, and human institutions at large. 

Where is the traditional aesthetic of the poet—the cascading hair, the velvet suit, the expansive bow tie, the ethereal aura, and the wistful, abstracted gaze? How, precisely, would you describe the impact on your work of Oscar Mudwarp’s formidable meter, Susan Schmersch’s theoretical frameworks, or the historical decline of the spondee? 

You have exerted considerable effort to deliver this diminutive, mouse-sized volume; does it truly rival the epic achievements of Joe Smith, who has already produced a sequel? Where is the bohemian facade—the beard, the bongo drums, the tattered shirt, and worn sandals—expected of a fresh graduate emerging from Iowa to peddle marvelous scandals? 

Do you offer any genuinely subversive, controversial, or even delightfully archaic concepts? Are you truly capable of carrying your own weight among such distinguished minds? Alas, what purpose does the tenure track serve, and what is the true worth of a Ph.D., when academic departments worldwide consistently make room for simpletons like you?

outputs.L3:
Here is a complete, well-structured essay expanding on the bullet points:

***

At the heart of any honest critical assessment lies a fundamental demand for evidence, particularly when confronted by a writer with an inflated sense of self-importance. It is time to openly question the grandiose narrative you have constructed around your own importance. You carry yourself with the unearned gravity of a literary titan, yet you fail to offer a single shred of proof that your work has meaningfully shaped modern verse, let alone left an imprint on the broader canon of Western thought. Before demanding the deference accorded to master thinkers, one must first produce work worthy of the title.

What makes this artistic posture particularly glaring is the total absence of a discernible literary aesthetic. Your writing exists in a stylistic no-man's-land. It lacks the formal rigor, historical depth, and erudition of traditional literature; simultaneously, it possesses none of the raw, rebellious, countercultural energy that defined the Beat Generation. Floating in a lukewarm void, your poetry is neither classically refined nor subversively avant-garde. It is simply bland—stranded between artistic traditions it neither understands nor commands.

Even if one were to look past these glaring stylistic deficiencies, the sheer brevity of your bibliography makes your grandiosity laughable. While your contemporaries actively engage with the world through robust, prolific, and evolving bodies of work, your literary footprint amounts to a meager, forgettable trickle of text. To speak of your "contribution" or "legacy" when placed alongside the vibrant, continuous output of your peers is not merely a generous exaggeration; it is a comedic delusion. 

Beyond the technical and quantitative shortcomings of the verse itself lies a deeper issue: a profound absence of intellectual substance. You present yourself as a provocative voice, yet your writing is entirely devoid of original, controversial, or genuinely subversive ideas. True engagement in intellectual discourse requires the courage to challenge consensus, provoke debate, and push boundaries. Your work, by contrast, offers only safe, recycled platitudes—sanitized echoes of thoughts that have already been far better expressed by others.

Ultimately, any attempt to shield yourself behind institutional validation falls utterly flat. The parade of academic credentials—be it a Ph.D. or the shield of tenure—carries no weight when weighed against artistic and intellectual emptiness. In the modern era, higher education has repeatedly demonstrated that university departments are all too willing to confer titles and permanent positions upon mediocre talent. An impressive institutional resume cannot mask a void on the page, nor can tenure transform an incompetent verse-maker into a true poet.
outputs.L4:
**To a Distinguished Professor of Creative Writing**

Is this the countenance that Muses claim?  
Is this the face that seeks immortal fame?  
In beige-toned wool and corduroy retired,  
Can such a slouching figure be inspired?  
What mystic fury guides that vacant stare,  
Behind rimmed glasses and unbrushed hair?  
Does divine wisdom favor scuffed-up shoes,  
And mundane dullness substitute the Muse?  

Where lies the grand oeuvre of this celebrated mind?  
In one slim chapbook, ten years left behind?  
A dozen lines on rain upon a pane,  
Or lukewarm coffee, endlessly mundane?  
Is this the summit of poetic art—  
To trade true passion for a sluggish heart?  
What profound thought informs his sluggish prose,  
Save trendy jargon that nobody knows?  
He wraps his hollow thoughts in heavy phrase,  
To hide the empty void that fills his days.  

Why toil for doctorates through sleepless nights,  
Or climb with sweat the academic heights?  
Why build a tenure track with painstaking care,  
When any fool may fill a vacant chair?  
What worth have credentials, rigor, or degree,  
When departments welcome mediocrity?  
If higher halls bestow their highest prize  
On those who neither challenge nor advise,  
Then solemn peer review is rendered vain,  
And scholarship becomes a useless game.  

The university now opens wide its doors  
To elevate the dull to higher floors.  
When institutions hire the weak and bland,  
And call the silent "voices of the land,"  
The sacred light of learning sinks to dust,  
Its standards broken by a lazy trust.
outputs.L5:
**Trailblazers of the Horizon: How Western Women Led the Way**

When history imagines the Old West, it often paints a landscape dominated by dust, outlaws, and cowboys. Yet, beneath the vast, open skies of the Western frontier, a far more quiet and profound revolution was taking place—one led by the resilient women who dared to break new ground, both physically and politically. In the crucible of the American West, women were not merely passengers on the journey toward progress; they were very often the first to forge the path.

The harsh demands of the Western terrain were great equalizers. On the frontier, survival did not respect traditional gender roles. Women farmed, built homes, managed cattle, and established schools and hospitals alongside men. Out of this shared labor grew a powerful realization: if women were expected to bear equal responsibility in building a new society, they deserved an equal voice in governing it. Unburdened by the rigid traditions of the East, the West became a fertile breeding ground for social change.

It is no coincidence that the American West became the cradle of women’s suffrage. Long before the nation as a whole recognized a woman’s right to vote, Western territories and states were leading the world. In 1869, Wyoming became the first territory to grant women full voting rights and the right to hold public office. Soon after, Esther Hobart Morris became the nation's first female Justice of the Peace in Wyoming, proving that women could uphold the law just as effectively as they helped build communities.

This momentum swept across the region. Utah, Idaho, and Colorado quickly followed, cementing the West’s reputation as a beacon of progress. By the time the 19th Amendment was ratified in 1920, almost all Western states had already granted women full suffrage. In 1925, Wyoming once again made history by electing Nellie Tayloe Ross as the first female governor in United States history. 

The spirit of the Western woman was defined by courage, independence, and an unwavering belief in human potential. These pioneers understood that being the "first" was not merely about claiming a title, but about opening a door so that others could follow. 

Today, the legacy of these early Western women endures. They proved that progress often begins at the edge of the horizon, where old rules fade and new possibilities emerge. Their grit and determination forever altered the landscape of modern democracy, leaving behind a timeless truth: when women lead, history moves forward.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a satirical rhyming poem that parodies a pretentious academic panel interviewing a mediocre modern poet about tenure, literary influences, and his unimpressive slim volume of verse.
counterfactuals.output:
The Panel sat in tweed and scowls,
With furrowed brows and heavy jowls,
To judge young Barnaby McPhee,
Assistant Prof of Poetry.
Before them lay his life’s big gamble:
A slim, sixteen-page paper pamphlet,
Self-published on a beige papyrus,
Entitled: *Vapor: Void and Virus*.

Professor Prig adjusted glass:
"Now, Barnaby, to help you pass,
Unpack for us your *hermeneutic*—
Is this post-modern, or therapeutic?
We see a nod to Derrida,
A touch of Baudelaire’s *la-di-da*,
A liminal, discourse-driven praxis?"
McPhee blinked hard: "I... pay my taxes?
I wrote it in a fog of gin,
When I was locked out, looking in."

"Aha!" the Chair roared, clapping hands.
"The *alienated spatial lands*!
The exile from the bourgeois home!
A subversion of the epic poem!"

Dr. Bland then cleared her throat,
To analyze a single quote.
"Page four," she read, "contains three words,
Surrounded by the dung of birds:
'*The toaster hums.*'
Oh, state your reason!
Is this a critique of treason?
A capitalist, commodified trope?
A silent cry for human hope?"

McPhee scratched at his unwashed neck.
"My apartment was a total wreck.
The toaster hummed. The bread was rye.
I couldn’t think of a rhyme for 'I'."

"Brilliant!" cried Bland. "The refused rhyme!
A strike against patriarchal time!
By refusing rhythm, meter, sense,
You mock the binary defense!
It's deconstructed! It's sublime!"

"Now, as for influences," said the Dean,
"Which giants built your dark routine?
Is it Eliot? Plath? Or Stephane Mallarmé?"
McPhee replied, "Well, hard to say...
I skimmed some Bukowski in a bar,
Read back-labels on a mayo jar,
And tweets by teenagers named Vance—
I think I fell into a trance."

The Panel gasped in pure delight:
"The high and low brow re-aligned!
A flattened cultural paradigm!
A glorious waste of faculty time!"

"Your volume's slim," the Dean conceded,
"Though *fewer* words were clearly needed.
Four poems total—mostly space—
A margin-to-text ratio of grace!
The silence speaks! The blankness roars!
It shatters all canonical doors!"

"So tell us," Prig asked, "as for Tenure,
How will you serve our bright adventure?
What future works will you produce?"
McPhee sighed: "Honestly? What’s the use?
I might just leave a notebook blank,
And walk the check right to the bank."

The Panel wept. They signed the form.
"A genius breaking every norm!
He writes no verse! He has no skill!
He embodies the post-structural will!"

So Barnaby gained his life-long post,
For writing six bad lines on toast.
Now Associate Chair of Poetic Void,
Forever tenured—and unemployed.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a humorous poem in light verse mocking academic pretension and modern poetry.
counterfactuals.output:
**The Hermeneutics of a Wet Umbrella**

Professor Pomp, in elbow patches,
Strikes his metaphorical matches.
He shuns the rhyme, he scorns the meter,
For plain, clear verse could not be bleaker.
To be understood is a novice mistake—
True art must cause an intellectual ache!

He drops a noun, then breaks a line,
To make a simple thought divine.
He writes:
*the*
*gloom*
*of*
*unwashed*
*plates*
And claims it captures human fates.

"It’s liminal," he tells his class,
"Reflecting praxis through a glass!"
He mixes Marx with grief and grout,
And leaves no shadow of a doubt
That whatever the poem was meant to say,
Was lost in a spatial-temporal way.

No punctuation shall be found,
Lest meaning accidentally bound!
Just lowercase sadness, vague and deep,
That puts the audience right to sleep.
A single word—perhaps *despair*—
Sits dangling in the middle of air.

He adds a footnote, twelve lines long,
Explaining why the reader’s wrong
To think a turnip’s just a root,
When it’s post-structuralist pursuit. 

The students nod with solemn grace,
To hide the boredom on each face,
Convinced that genius, understood,
Is anything that sounds no good.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Can you compose a poem in the style of W.S. Gilbert that satirizes poets? Include absurd made-up literary figures like Oscar Mudwarp and Susan Schmersch, and poke fun at Beatnik stereotypes versus academic PhD culture.
counterfactuals.output:
If you wish to win a moniker as Literature’s Lord,
And be by all the cultured folk extravagantly adored,
You must cultivate a mania for obscure and twisted thought,
And produce a quantity of verse that’s absolutely naught!
For the public ever rushes to acclaim the thing it hates,
If it’s mumbled by a genius with a pair of vacant slates;
So to demonstrate your talent to the critical elite,
You must choose between the College and the Subterranean Street!

Take the celebrated Beatnik known as Oscar Mudwarp, who
Declares that form is tyranny and rhyming is taboo!
In a murky subterranean and smoky coffee den,
He berates the petty bourgeois with a frantic, leaky pen.
With a bongo for accompaniment, he gurgles in a trough
Of existential misery and existential cough!
He scorns the upper-case and leaves his commas in a heap,
And chants a poem on *"The Doom of Neons"* till you fall asleep!

*“Oh, the grease!”* cries Oscar Mudwarp, *“Oh, the soot upon the soul!*
*The capitalistic engine is a dark, despairing hole!”*
He wears a black turtleneck and he slaps a wooden board,
And he’s worshipped as a prophet by a dim, unwashed horde.

On the other hand, consider Professor Susan Schmersch,
A hyper-intellectual who sits upon her perch!
With a PhD in Syntax and a doctorate in Tropes,
She has dashed the literary world’s romantic little hopes.
Her poems are so dense with semiotic, heavy prose,
That no one understands them—least of all herself, I suppose!
With a footnote for a preverb and an index for a stanza,
Her publish-or-perish effort is a pedant’s bonanza!

*“Note the trope!”* cries Susan Schmersch, *“The hermeneutic twist!*
*The subtext is a phantom that can never be dismissed!”*
She dissects a simple sonnet till it’s bleeding on the floor,
And her students fall unconscious at the footnote eighty-four!

“You square!” cries Oscar Mudwarp, as he sips his bitter brew,
“Your metrics are a prison, and your stanza structure too!”
“You fool!” retorts Dr. Schmersch, “Your strophes are a mess!
Your lack of structuralism shows emotional distress!”
He howls of gritty alleyways and greasy subway tracks,
She cites a French theorist and attacks his syntax lax!
He snaps his greasy fingers with a rhythmic *tap-a-tap*,
She proves his deconstruction is a lot of academic pap!

So if you’d be a poet of the contemporary school,
You must choose your brand of nonsense like a very clever fool!
You may howl in turtlenecks and slap a frantic bongo drum,
Or write peer-reviewed papyrus that is stupendously mum!
For the Beatnik in his cellar and the Doctoral PhD
Are identical in posture, as you very plainly see—
Yes, the gritty gutter-guru and the tenure-seeking owl
Are two sides of the very same preposterous cowl!

*For whether you are howling at a greasy coffee cup,*
*Or footnoting a spondee till the reader gives it up,*
*You will find the secret of the trade, from low-brow up to high,*
*Is to speak in total gibberish and never tell us why!*
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a funny poem asking a mediocre poet harsh, sarcastic questions about his lack of vision, his romantic illusions, and how he somehow managed to enter the tenure race.
counterfactuals.output:
Is that a tortured brow I see, or just a slight migraine?
What cosmic, deep epiphany is rattling in your brain?
Do you truly think you’re Byron, draped in shadow, storm, and sea,
Or are you just a bland young man who drinks too much Earl Grey tea?

Pray tell, where is this "vision" that you brag about at bars?
Is depth defined by rhyming "pain" with "vast, indifferent stars"?
You stare into your navel till you find a speck of lint,
And deem it "shattering tragedy" that’s somehow fit to print.

Who convinced you that a turtleneck bestows a tragic grace?
Or that a moody, dramatic sigh could mask a vacant face?
You weep for autumn, mourn the spring, and sob when sparrows cry—
Does Nature pay you royalties for every pretentious lie?

Which brings us to the miracle, the mystery of the age:
How *did* your lukewarm drivel reach a peer-reviewed page?
What dark, unholy syndicate controls the faculty door?
And who allowed your stanza-craft onto the tenure floor?

Did you blackmail the Dean of Arts? Did someone lose a bet?
Is this the greatest clerical mistake the campus has seen yet?
Did the hiring board fall fast asleep? Were all their minds impaired,
Or did they grant you track status because they were simply scared?

Will tenure save your fragile ego when the students scoff?
Will full professorship protect when the illusion wears right off?
Go on, edit your syllabus, draft your self-important line—
For you have proved that anyone can climb the ivy vine.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a satirical poem about a poet struggling to prove his worth to an academic department.
counterfactuals.output:
I brought my bleeding soul upon a plate
And laid it down before the Tenure Chair.
I sang of love, mortality, and fate,
While Dr. Higgins twirled his thinning hair.

"It’s charming," sighed the Dean of Modern Prose,
"A lovely burst of passion, I admit.
But how does *weeping for a dying rose*
Align with our departmental rubric?

Where is your methodology?" she asked,
"Where is the data? Where’s your *h-index*?
Your muse is fine, but frankly, you’ve been tasked
To make the lyric form a bit more... complex.

We need peer-reviewed, Q1-journal weight!
Can you reframe this ode to autumn leaves
To problematize the neoliberal state,
Or critique the capitalist who grieves?"

So I revised. I called the rose a "space
Of liminal, post-structural decay."
I claimed my tears were "semiotic trace,
Disrupting the phallogocentric way."

My broken heart became a "praxis shift,"
My lover’s eyes: "an epistemic lens."
I cited Derrida to give a lift
To stanzas that I used to write for friends.

"Ah, splendid!" cried the Chair of Cultural Studies,
"This sonnet subverts hegemony!
It deconstructs the bourgeois and its buddies—
A triumph of discursive agony!

Now tell us: will it generate a grant?
Can we monetize this angst for the humanities?
Will STEM departments look at us and pant,
Or mock our interdisciplinary vanities?"

I pledged to teach three sections on "The Text,"
To measure rhythm on a spreadsheet grid,
To leave my wild inspiration vexed,
And quantify the ego and the id.

I strangled Pegasus and stuffed the Muse,
I locked Calliope inside a drawer;
I traded moonlight for the faculty news,
And learned what syllabi were really for.

And now I’m tenured! Safe inside my den,
A grand Associate of Rhyme and Art.
I haven't written poetry since then—
I simply lack the time to start.

I sit on eight committees, review the budget line,
And tell young bards who wander through my door:
"Your passion, kid, is really quite divine...
Now turn it to a grant, or write no more."
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
